plan.purpose: Help an agent-systems architect recognise when context isolation removes the comparison set required for relational global prioritization, distinguish missing-context indiscrimination from default-driven failure direction, and see the architectural trade-offs of splitting narrow-deep execution from wide-shallow triage.
must-keep: When the right allocation or escalation decision changes with live competing work and no locally comparable live signal enters the worker, isolating context for task focus removes the live comparison set relational global prioritization requires.

Missing competing-work context alone causes priority indiscrimination; it does not by itself set the direction of failure (over-escalation versus silent continuation), which requires a separate mechanism.
Standing priority rules in static context cannot order a local branch against unseen live competing work across a changing workload.
Splitting narrow-deep execution from wide-shallow triage relocates the trade-off to the summary boundary between views rather than eliminating it.
